summary: Preserved candidate 49a136764025c3a0ac76b2105884bbf1215e1e0b: safe decode-prefix Mamba eviction is default-on while admission-safe pool ratios remain 3/4/5. Independent base/candidate runs verify both fixes. The review's unreclaimable 2N boundary was reproduced: it makes one eviction attempt and raises synchronously, while 3N and decode-evictable 2N succeed. No further source change is justified without a faithful scheduler/HiCache hybrid-Mamba reproduction.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before: 8 passed and 2 failed; decode lock skipping was default-off and the enabled lazy ratio was 3 instead of the admission-safe 4.
10 focused cases, including one-attempt locked 2N exhaustion, 3N success, decode-evictable 2N recovery, default-on behavior, admission ratios, lock symmetry, and PP sizing.
17 allocation-aware unified-cache eviction boundary cases passed.
8 tests and 542 request/token-boundary subtests passed; this suite does not establish HTTP responsiveness under Mamba pressure.

gpu_execution.evidence: The verified behavior is CPU-side scheduler/cache accounting. No compatible hybrid-Mamba model workload was available; a generic GPU smoke would not qualify the issue.

remaining_limitations: No scheduler/HTTP regression proves graceful request rejection or completion responsiveness for an unreclaimable Mamba admission.
The zero-running post-flush exhaustion state was not reproduced or explained.
Direct hierarchical-cache I/O blocking and the reported 222-second TTFT were not reproduced.
Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP=8, H100/CUDA, EAGLE, 100K+ production traffic, and model semantics remain unverified.
The tiny Llama fixture cannot exercise a hybrid-Mamba allocator and is not evidence for this issue.
